phenotype_specificity.statement: P3 and P4 (PMID 33391282) are in the severe LAD1° class with umbilical cord separation recorded as "Yes" and omphalitis, features the paper names as typical. Only ITGB2 was sequenced (Sanger) for LAD1 patients; no other genes reported as tested. A0096 and A0120 have no clinical data.

| LAD1<sup>o</sup> | P4 | ♀ | 0.3 | 24 | Yes | Omphalitis, skin rash | Yes | No | *-* | 22980 | Expired |
These patients usually present in infancy with delayed separation of the umbilical cord, omphalitis, and necrotic infections of the skin and mucosal surfaces (5).
Molecular confirmation was performed was done using Sanger sequencing for LAD1 and next-generation sequencing (NGS) for LAD3.

segregation.statement: No relatives were genotyped in either paper. P4 has a positive family history; P3 does not; no carrier status of relatives is given.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Batch HGVS: nonsense, p.(Tyr544Ter), agreeing with both papers (p.Tyr544X; p.Tyr544Ter). The paper describes the disease as caused by decreased expression or function of CD18.

quotes.quote: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by decreased expression or functioning of CD18, the β_2 subunit of the leukocyte β_2 integrins [1].
Usually, this leads to the absence or decreased expression of the β_2 integrins on the leukocyte surface, but sometimes a normal expression of nonfunctional β_2 integrins is found.

Direct Sanger sequencing of the ITGβ2 gene revealed 57 disease-causing variants in 105 patients (Table S2), including 30 patients we have previously reported (18).

concerns: PMID 22134107 is a mutation-update table (Table I) without case descriptions: people are identified only by database accession numbers, and sex, age and clinical features are not given per person.

In Table I the LAD-I type and the families (alleles) count belong to the table row (the variant), not to one accession number; for an accession number listed with a second variant, the expression class reflects the person's genotype, not this allele alone.

Possible same-person duplicates: A0096 and A0120 were unpublished in the 2011/2012 table, whose authors include Dr Manisha Madkaikar, who is also an author of the 2020 Indian cohort (PMID 33391282). The table's 2 families (3 alleles) matches one person with two copies plus one heterozygous person, as with P3 (not marked heterozygous) and P4 (heterozygous). Neither paper links the accession numbers to P3 or P4, so this is unconfirmed.
P4 has a second ITGB2 variant (c.1828C>A, p.Pro610Thr).
For A0096 and A0120, the table does not say which person has two copies or what the other allele of the heterozygous person is.
notes_for_panel: If A0096/A0120 are P3/P4, there are two carriers rather than four.
